---
description: map_measure as the model is told it - what the tool does, and what each of its arguments is.
doing: measuring on a map
arguments:
  at: "The place whose map to measure on; leave it out when from names someone or something on a map."
  from: "Where to measure from: someone or something on the map, or a square [column, row]."
  to: "Where to measure to, the same way: gives the distance, whether the two see each other, the cover the one has from the other, and the way between with its cost and time."
  within: "A range in squares: who and what stands within it of from."
  area: "An area that starts at from: burst (a radius all round it), cone, line or cube. Where it starts and how much of a square it must cover to count are the world's ruleset's to say, else the settings'; D&D's grid rule starts it at a point where squares meet and counts a square covered by half."
  size: "The area's size in squares: a burst's radius, a cone's or a line's length, a cube's side."
  toward: "Where a cone, a line or a cube points: someone or something on the map, or a square."
  speed: "Squares the mover covers in a round, for the way's time; the map's own when left out."
---
Measures on a place's map of squares as play stands now: the distance between two spots in squares and feet; whether they see each other (walls, doors that are not open and whatever blocks the view stop it); the cover one has from the other (half, three-quarters or total, by what stands across the lines between their corners, and what it is); the way between them, what it costs and how long it takes; who and what stands within a range; and the squares a burst, a cone, a line or a cube covers, as runs by row, with who stands in it. Someone who stands on no square is said to, with where they are kept (a zone or words), and the rest is measured. It changes nothing.
